title: Global Semiconductor Sales Increase 35.1% from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026
gist: The Semiconductor Industry Association's August 6, 2026 release puts Q2 2026 global chip sales at $403.3 billion, 35.1% above Q1 2026, with June alone at $134.5 billion — 123.6% above June 2025. Regional year-over-year growth ran from 160.9% in the Americas to 39% in Japan, and SIA CEO John Neuffer guided to full-year 2026 sales above $1.5 trillion.

insights.claim: The Semiconductor Industry Association reported global semiconductor sales of $403.3 billion in Q2 2026, up 35.1% from Q1 2026.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: Annualizing a $403.3 billion quarter implies a run-rate above $1.6 trillion, which is the number to test against equipment and materials order books.
insights.quote: global semiconductor sales were $403.3 billion during the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 35.1% compared to Q1 of 2026

insights.claim: June 2026 global chip sales of $134.5 billion were 123.6% higher than June 2025 and 9.7% higher than May 2026.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: More than doubling year-over-year while still adding ~10% month-over-month means the cycle had not yet decelerated as of June — no rollover signal in the data.
insights.quote: Global sales were $134.5 billion during the month of June 2026, an increase of 123.6% compared to June 2025 and 9.7% more than sales in May 2026.

insights.claim: The reported monthly figures are World Semiconductor Trade Statistics data expressed as a three-month moving average, so any single monthly print blends three months of activity.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: Treat the monthly series as a smoothed trend indicator, not a real-time demand reading — inflections show up late.

insights.claim: SIA president and CEO John Neuffer said global chip sales are expected to exceed $1.5 trillion in 2026, with Q2 substantially outpacing Q1 2026.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: A $1.5 trillion-plus industry sets the denominator for market-share and TAM math across foundries, equipment vendors and IP suppliers this year.
insights.quote: Global chip sales are expected to exceed $1.5 trillion in 2026, with Q2 sales substantially outpacing sales in Q1 2026

insights.claim: Neuffer attributes growth to strong sales across the Americas, Asia Pacific and China, framing semiconductors as central to the next generation of technology innovation and economic competitiveness.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: The industry body is positioning chip demand as strategically essential, language that supports continued policy and subsidy backing.

insights.claim: Year-over-year June sales growth was led by the Americas at 160.9%, followed by Asia Pacific/All Other at 124.4%, China at 112.8%, Europe at 75.2% and Japan at 39%.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: The Americas growing roughly four times faster than Japan points to where the incremental demand — and the associated regional supply-chain build-out — is concentrated.
insights.quote: year-to-year sales in June were up in the Americas (160.9%), Asia Pacific/All Other (124.4%), China (112.8%), Europe (75.2%), and Japan (39%)

insights.claim: Every region posted month-over-month June growth within a narrow 7.7% to 10.4% band — China 10.4%, Asia Pacific/All Other 9.8%, the Americas 9.6%, Japan 8.6% and Europe 7.7%.
insights.speaker: O
insights.so_what: Synchronized sequential growth across all regions argues the current momentum is broad demand rather than a narrow AI-datacenter or single-geography effect.
insights.quote: Month-to-month sales in June increased in China (10.4%), Asia Pacific/All Other (9.8%), the Americas (9.6%), Japan (8.6%), and Europe (7.7%).
